newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UNSETTLED GINOLA HINTS AT MOVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNSETTLED GINOLA HINTS AT MOVE.

text.p: David Ginola has given a veiled warning to his manager Kenny Dalglish that he does not intend to stay at Newcastle if he is left on the substitutes' bench.

On the day the English premier league team faced Monaco in the home leg of their UEFA Cup quarter-final, the 30-year-old Frenchman said on the Clubcall service: "We have an important game on Tuesday and I don't want to think about my future just now.
"But I didn't come to Newcastle to be a substitute and if the manager doesn't put you in the team you maybe have to say bye-bye.
"I don't want to put pressure on the manager but if I don't play in team it's a shame for me. I want to be more involved."
The winger has been out of favour in recent weeks and started on the bench against Southampton on Saturday.
He came on as a second-half substitute for Les Ferdinand and is likely to be asked to play the centre forward role again against Monaco as Dalglish faces a striker shortage.
Alan Shearer is out after a groin operation, Ferdinand is doubtful with a hamstring strain and Faustino Asprilla is suspended.
Ginola has played in the position for Paris Saint-Germain and said: "It is a very big problem for us and if I can help the team like that I will."
